question.text:
When two sound waves travel in the same direction in a medium, the displacements of a particle located at ' $x$ ' at time ' $t$ ' is given by :
$\begin{aligned}
& y_1=0.05 \cos (0.50 \pi x-100 \pi t) \\
& y_2=0.05 \cos (0.46 \pi x-92 \pi t)
\end{aligned}$
where $y_1, y_2$ and $x$ are in meters and $t$ in seconds. 
The speed of sound in the medium is :

solution.text:
Standard equation
$y(x, t)=A \cos \left(\frac{\omega}{V} x-\omega t\right)$
From any of the displacement equation 
Say $\mathrm{y}_1$
$\frac{\omega}{\mathrm{V}}=0.50 \pi$ and $\omega=100 \pi$
$\therefore \frac{100 \pi}{\mathrm{V}}=0.5 \pi$
$\therefore \mathrm{V}=\frac{100 \pi}{0.5 \pi}=200 \mathrm{~m} / \mathrm{s}$
